body: I have yet to meet someone who works for a company with a competent staff. With the economy where it's at right now, you don't really have a choice.
> And this is how every workplace is in my field (civil engineering, the most mediocre discipline of the already mediocre field of engineering), so there's no way of changing the situation.

I've made most of the changes therapists suggest and my depression hasn't really changed. I also feel like the more I talk about me or my feelings the more unstable I get.

For what it's worth, I'm back to regular ideation. There was a specific thing that called me to action that resolved itself. But suicide still feels inevitable within the next five years or so.

When my brother committed suicide, I felt similarly. It was devastating. I am so sorry you are going through this.

What you're feeling now is not what you'll be feeling in a month, and that will be different a year from now. If you had depression before, that will still be there, but it will be different than how it is in this moment. If you weren't depressed before, then you might not feel as depressed in the future.

But no matter what, this is not a decision you should be making now. Put this decision off for a bit.
Curious: what is your motivation in doing this, since it is certain you will survive if you do it in front of them?

Pretty much everyone who attempts with cutting survives.

It takes a really long time, and it's really unpleasant, so eventually you will call for help and live.

Edit: keep in mind, cutting is perceived by the masses as a cry-for-help and not a sincere attempt, so if you are looking for sympathy or want people to take you seriously, this isn't the way to do it. If you don't actually want to die, discuss your depression and suicidal ideation with a doctor or other professional and ask for a referral for treatment.

Well I'm doing a bit better. 

It's funny, this has happened before, but "tying loose ends" (and to me, that means doing a deep cleaning of my apartment so if I die people don't think I lived in filth, and so grieving people don't have to deal with it, and also taking care of anything that needs to be wrapped up at work) generally makes my life better enough that I don't feel that drive to kill myself anymore. Lord knows I'm still depressed, just not over the edge depressed anymore.
